note: The only broker call today is the Tokyo Cement earnings note (prices as of 9 November). The Singer and Jetwing Symphony cards are results summaries, not new ratings. Foreign flow figures per stock are read from the snapshot chart's bar labels. The X thread on why the Iran war hit Sri Lankan shares was only linked, not posted, so only its teaser is summarised. Two images were decorative (a news banner and a stock-chart photo).
highlights: A very strong day: the ASPI jumped 2.75% (592 points) and the S&P SL20 3.66% on Rs 7.9bn turnover, led by Commercial Bank, Dialog, HNB, Hayleys and Vallibel One.

Foreign investors sold a net Rs 1.2bn, almost all of it in Dialog (about Rs 1.0bn), even though Dialog's price rose 4.9%. The site's Dialog fair value (Rs 31) is still well below the broker's last target (Rs 55).
Singer rose 6.5% to Rs 79.90, close to the broker's Rs 85 target but nearly double the site's fair value of Rs 42.3. September-quarter sales rose 21%, but earnings per share fell 6% to Rs 1.16.
Tokyo Cement: the broker keeps Buy with targets of Rs 120 (voting) and Rs 104 (non-voting) but changed its short-term outlook to Negative after margins fell.
Oil fell sharply after the US signalled it would hold off on new strikes on Iran, and world markets rallied.

news.title: Tokyo Cement September quarter
news.text: Sales rose 28% to Rs 20.9bn on a price increase in April and about 12% higher volumes, and market share rose to 34%. Dearer clinker and a weaker rupee cut the gross margin to 28%, and profit for shareholders fell 13% to Rs 866mn. Return on equity is 7.7%. The broker expects a softer December quarter and says margins must recover before returns improve.

news.title: Singer September quarter
news.text: Sales rose 21% to Rs 35.7bn, but earnings per share fell to Rs 1.16 from Rs 1.23. The broker puts the shares at 11.8 times trailing earnings and 4.2 times book value.

news.title: Jetwing Symphony September quarter
news.text: Sales rose 8% to Rs 1.28bn and earnings per share were Rs 0.35, against Rs 0.39 a year earlier. The shares trade at 17.7 times trailing earnings and 1.9 times book value.

news.title: Government budget in surplus
news.text: The budget showed a Rs 22.3bn surplus for the first nine months of 2026, against a Rs 441bn deficit a year earlier. Revenue rose 20%, helped by taxes on vehicle imports.

news.title: Bank lending outpacing deposits
news.text: Banks' loans reached 74% of deposits at the end of June, the first time above 70% in three years. The Central Bank warned that loans growing faster than deposits could become a risk.

news.title: HNB partners with IFC
news.text: HNB and the World Bank's IFC will work together to expand supply chain finance and improve HNB's risk management.

news.title: JKH and the port terminal
news.text: JKH is still waiting for the government to decide what happens to its SAGT terminal when the concession ends in 2029: a handover, a new tender or an extension.

news.title: Hayleys supermarkets and tourism
news.text: Hayleys Retail chose Blue Yonder's software to build a new grocery chain. Tourist arrivals passed 1.9 million this year but are behind last year's pace.

news.title: Sri Lankan shares and the Iran war
news.text: A broker thread says the ASPI has been one of 2026's worst markets because of the Iran war, and that one factor will decide the recovery. Oil fell more than $7 a barrel after the US said it would hold off on new strikes, and US and Asian indices rose about 2–4%.
